thesisQuality.note: Realized leading-edge growth, extraordinary margins, massive self-funded capex capacity and centrality to advanced semiconductor manufacturing support an exceptional thesis; geopolitical and concentration risks prevent a maximum.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 revenue rose 36.0% YoY and 12.0% sequentially while net income rose 77.4% YoY; gross and operating margins reached 67.7% and 60.3%.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: At $430.26 and roughly $2.0T market capitalization, trailing P/E near 28.3x and forward P/E near 19.5x are not distressed but remain moderate relative to current growth and profitability; geopolitical tail risk warrants conservatism.

catalystScore.note: Q3 guidance calls for $44.6B-$45.8B revenue and a steep 2nm ramp after 2nm already reached 3% of Q2 wafer revenue, creating a near-term measurable catalyst.

governancePower.note: A ten-member globally experienced board with multiple independent directors provides oversight, while combined Chairman/CEO authority at C.C. Wei reduces structural separation and caps the assessment.

alignment2036.note: TSMC is foundational manufacturing infrastructure for advanced compute, AI, communications and heterogeneous semiconductor systems; 77% of Q2 wafer revenue came from 7nm-and-below technologies.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Leading-edge process manufacturing serves multiple compute, communications and semiconductor end markets and compounds ecosystem leverage across successive nodes.

bottleneckControl.note: The steep 2nm ramp and 77% advanced-node mix evidence direct control over scarce leading-edge fabrication capacity that constrains advanced computing supply.

scenarioRobustness.note: Broad end-market exposure, exceptional profitability and large liquidity support resilience across demand scenarios; geographic/geopolitical concentration materially limits robustness.

substitutionResilience.note: Successive leading-edge node ramps, advanced-node revenue dominance and extreme capital intensity create high substitution barriers, though Samsung/Intel foundry and customer vertical integration remain credible alternatives.

supplyChainResilience.note: NT$3.5T cash and marketable securities plus very strong operating cash flow support redundancy and capacity investment, but Taiwan-centered leading-edge manufacturing and equipment/material dependencies remain material concentration risks.

pricingPower.note: Q2 gross margin of 67.7% and operating margin of 60.3% alongside 36% YoY revenue growth demonstrate exceptional economics and pricing/mix power at leading-edge nodes.

risk.note: Exceptional liquidity, margins and node leadership offset major Taiwan geopolitical/geographic concentration, cyclicality, enormous capital intensity, customer concentration and alternative-foundry risks.

confidence.note: Current primary quarterly operating evidence and governance material cover the required operating/governance factors, with current independent market data for valuation; detailed customer/supplier concentration and geopolitical scenario probabilities remain explicit non-gating unknowns.

thesis: TSMC combines exceptional realized financial momentum with dominant control of leading-edge fabrication bottlenecks and a steep 2nm ramp, making it foundational to 2036 compute infrastructure; geopolitical concentration is the principal structural counterweight.
keyRisk: A Taiwan geopolitical disruption, geographic manufacturing concentration, customer/platform concentration or successful foundry substitution could impair a business whose valuation now reflects substantial continued leadership.
nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 results and 2nm ramp evidence against management's $44.6B-$45.8B revenue and 65%-67% gross-margin guidance.
